questions.prompt: What is the role of a hash function in a hash table?

options.text: To map keys deterministically to bucket indices distributed as uniformly as possible

questions.prompt: What happens when a hash table's load factor (entries / buckets) grows too high?

options.text: The hash function changes to O(log n)
Lookups degrade toward O(n) due to collisions until the table resizes and rehashes

questions.prompt: Select the two primary collision-resolution strategies used in hash tables. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Open addressing (linear/quadratic probing or Robin Hood)

questions.prompt: What does the Go map lookup `val, ok := counts[key]` prevent?

options.text: Confusing a missing key with a key whose stored value is the zero value

questions.prompt: In a Binary Search Tree (BST), which traversal visits all keys in sorted ascending order?
What is the worst-case search time of an unbalanced BST built from already-sorted keys?
When deleting a node with two children from a BST, what value replaces it?

options.text: Always the root of the tree
Either its in-order successor (min of right subtree) or in-order predecessor (max of left subtree)

questions.prompt: What invariant does a min-heap satisfy?

options.text: Every node is smaller than or equal to its children (root is the global minimum)
All leaves are at the same exact depth and sorted
The root is always the median

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of building a binary heap from an existing array of `n` elements (Floyd's bottom-up heapify)?
Which Go standard library package provides `Init`, `Push`, and `Pop` for priority queues?
To find the `k` largest elements in a stream of `n` numbers using O(k) memory, which heap should you maintain?

options.text: A min-heap of size k (popping the smallest whenever size exceeds k)

questions.prompt: Why does classic binary search write `mid := lo + (hi - lo)/2` instead of `(lo + hi)/2`?

options.text: It avoids signed integer overflow when `lo + hi` exceeds `math.MaxInt`
It rounds up instead of down

questions.prompt: What standard library function in Go performs binary search on a sorted slice or predicate?
What does 'binary search on the answer' require?

options.text: The input array must already be sorted
A hash table of all answers
A monotonic feasibility predicate `ok(x)` over a bounded answer range `[lo..hi]`

questions.prompt: Select all sorting algorithms that are **stable** in their standard implementations. (Select all that apply.)
Match each sorting algorithm to its worst-case time complexity.
In Go's `slices.SortFunc` / `sort.SliceStable`, why does `pdqsort` (pattern-defeating quicksort) outperform naive quicksort?

options.text: It allocates a new linked list per element
It uses counting sort for all structs
It combines quicksort, heapsort fallback on bad partitions, and insertion sort on tiny slices

questions.prompt: When representing a sparse graph (`|E| << |V|^2`), why is an adjacency list preferred over an adjacency matrix?

options.text: Adjacency lists use O(V + E) space instead of O(V^2) and iterate neighbors in O(deg(v))
Adjacency matrices cannot represent directed graphs
Adjacency lists give O(1) edge-existence queries
Adjacency matrices do not support weighted edges

questions.prompt: Which graph traversal guarantees finding the shortest path (fewest edges) in an **unweighted** graph?
What does Kahn's algorithm produce when run on a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)?

options.text: A topological ordering of vertices (and detects a cycle if fewer than V vertices are output)

questions.prompt: Which two optimizations make Union-Find (Disjoint Set Union) run in nearly O(1) amortized (`O(alpha(n))`) per operation? (Select all that apply.)
Under what condition can Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm produce an incorrect answer?

options.text: When the graph has cycles of positive weight
When the graph contains negative-weight edges

questions.prompt: What advantage does Bellman-Ford have over Dijkstra's algorithm?

options.text: It handles negative edge weights and can detect negative-weight cycles reachable from the source
It is faster on dense graphs

questions.prompt: In A* search, what property must the heuristic `h(n)` satisfy to guarantee an optimal shortest path?

options.text: `h(n)` must always overestimate the remaining cost
`h(n)` must be admissible (never overestimate the true remaining distance to the goal)
`h(n)` must equal 0 for all nodes only

questions.prompt: Match each graph algorithm to the problem it solves.
What is the time complexity of `TwoSum` on an unsorted slice of `n` integers using a hash map?

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(1) space

questions.prompt: What does `defer` in Go NOT fix when traversing a graph with DFS?

options.text: Preventing infinite loops on graphs with cycles — you still need a `visited` set

questions.prompt: In tree recursion, what is the height of a balanced binary tree with `n` nodes?
What is the purpose of a `visited` check *before* pushing onto a BFS queue (instead of only on pop)?

options.text: It prevents the same vertex from being enqueued multiple times, avoiding O(E) duplicate queue entries

questions.prompt: Which data structure is used to merge `k` sorted slices of total length `n` in `O(n log k)` time?

options.text: A hash table of size n
A min-heap of size k holding the current head element of each slice

questions.prompt: Select all statements that are true about Prim's and Kruskal's MST algorithms. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Both require all edge weights to be positive
Both find a Minimum Spanning Tree on a connected undirected weighted graph
Kruskal sorts edges and uses Union-Find to skip cycle-forming edges
Prim grows a single tree from a start vertex using a priority queue

questions.prompt: What is the result of `slices.BinarySearch([]int{2, 5, 8, 12}, 7)` in Go?

options.text: `2, false` (index 2 is where `7` would be inserted to stay sorted)

questions.prompt: When is Radix Sort faster than O(n log n) comparison sorts?

options.text: When keys are fixed-width integers or short strings so digit passes (`d`) are small
When keys are arbitrary custom structs with complex comparators

questions.prompt: What causes a hash map's `O(1)` lookup assumption to break in adversarial inputs?

options.text: Hash flooding (many keys colliding into the same bucket)

questions.prompt: What does this BFS loop compute when `dist[start] = 0` and all other `dist` entries start at `-1`?

options.text: Shortest hop distance from `start` to every reachable vertex

questions.prompt: Match each BST traversal order to its typical use case.

columns.label: Emit BST keys in sorted order
Bottom-up aggregation (height, subtree size, free nodes)

questions.prompt: How do you detect whether an undirected graph contains a cycle using Union-Find?

options.text: Check if any vertex has degree > 1
Run binary search on edge weights
If `find(u) == find(v)` when processing edge `(u, v)`, adding `(u, v)` closes a cycle

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of `mergeSort` on an array of `n` elements?

options.text: O(n log n) best, average, and worst case (with O(n) auxiliary space)

questions.prompt: Which properties hold for a valid Binary Search Tree (BST)? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Every subtree is itself a valid BST
The root must always be the middle index of the input array
All keys in the left subtree of `x` are strictly less than `x.Key` (assuming distinct keys)
All keys in the right subtree of `x` are greater than `x.Key`

questions.prompt: In `container/heap`, why does `Pop() any` remove from the end of the underlying slice?

options.text: The root is always at the end of the slice
`container/heap` swaps the root (index 0) with the last element and shrinks the heap before calling your `Pop()`
Slices only support popping at index 0

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of checking if a directed graph has a cycle using 3-color DFS (unvisited/visiting/done)?
Why is `quicksort` often faster in practice than `mergesort` for in-memory arrays despite having the same average O(n log n)?

options.text: Mergesort is O(n^2) on random data
Quicksort sorts in place with high cache locality and low memory traffic
